items.title: Uniform force offsets do not explain the archived common error
items.summary: Uniform offsets account for less than 0.000001 percent of common residual energy on MatPES and 0.01746 percent on OMat24, averaged with equal original group weights. Both panel means are below the fixed 50 percent threshold. The remaining shared error is atom dependent; this closes the archived diagnostic branch.
findings: The full-configuration projection splits common residual energy exactly into uniform-offset and atom-dependent components. All 800 configurations and 100 original groups were retained; no mask, rank or prediction was changed.

Primary averages use eight configuration fractions per group and fifty equal groups per panel. Secondary pooled offset shares are less than 0.000001 percent on MatPES and 0.002405 percent on OMat24; pooling weights by total common residual energy.
An independent exact-rational reconstruction passed 60,344 numeric comparisons, verified every decomposition and internal-vector zero sum, and found no zero denominator or decision discrepancy.
The final planned archive control is completed. Further empirical work must introduce new reference or predictor evidence under a separately justified design.
limitations: Repeatedly inspected historical data; no independent holdout, significance test, calibration, corrected model performance or generalization claim.
Atom-dependent reference mismatch and shared model limitations remain unresolved. Net-force vectors do not identify an offset origin; exact arithmetic is not physical provenance validation.
Tiny MatPES ratios are rounded as bounds and do not establish physical accuracy at that decimal precision. Historical checkpoint identity and training independence remain unresolved.

Raw artifacts stay private; published hashes identify them without supplying public reproduction inputs. Historical A6 remains INCONCLUSIVE and the independent MPtrj validation remains stopped before execution.
items.nextStep: Planned: investigate a bounded paired-reference microstudy on new exactly matched geometries. Source identity, geometry pairing, units, calculation conventions and prior-exposure exclusions must pass before freezing and executing the new comparison. No further decomposition of these 800 cases.

items.title: Shared aligned residuals carry most error on both archived panels
items.summary: Analysis of all 800 reused configurations passes the fixed criterion for both panel averages: aligned residuals carry 71.00 percent of ensemble squared error on MatPES and 76.52 percent on OMat24 with equal original group weights. Exact arithmetic independently confirmed this descriptive result; the cause of shared residuals remains unresolved.
findings: The sole fixed mask requires common residual energy to exceed model contrast and all three residual pair dot products to be positive. Both primary panel means exceed the fixed one-half threshold.
Pooled fractions of total ensemble squared error are 84.93 percent on MatPES and 86.84 percent on OMat24. Pooling weights configurations by their total error and differs from the primary average.

The mask contains 2,061 of 3,324 atoms on MatPES and 2,488 of 3,912 on OMat24. Individually, 306 of 400 MatPES configurations and 329 of 400 OMat24 configurations exceed the half threshold; all cases and groups were retained.

Independent exact-decimal reconstruction verified both identities for all 7,236 atoms and passed 292,766 numeric comparisons. There were no mask or decision discrepancies and no zero-error denominator cases.
limitations: Repeatedly inspected historical data; no independent holdout, significance test, calibration, new score, force-error reduction or generalization claim.
Shared model limitations and reference mismatch remain competing explanations. Model agreement does not identify the cause of common residuals or certify accuracy.
Historical predictor names do not establish exact checkpoints or training independence. Raw artifacts stay private; published hashes identify them without supplying public reproduction inputs.
No new predictions or candidate-data analysis occurred. Historical A6 remains INCONCLUSIVE and the proposed independent validation stays stopped before execution.
items.nextStep: One final archived control, planned: quantify uniform per-configuration force offsets using a full-configuration translation/internal decomposition with fixed group weighting. Then close this diagnostic branch regardless of outcome; further empirical progress must add new reference or predictor evidence.

items.title: Proposed independent validation stops at training-split eligibility
items.summary: A bounded source audit cannot establish that the pinned MPtrj candidate is held out from the three proposed checkpoints, or that its reference conventions are sufficiently documented. The proposed 128-group validation has stopped before selection or inference. This does not prove exact-row contamination or refute the ranking hypothesis.
findings: CHGNet 0.3.0 documents 90 percent training and 5 percent each for validation and test. Its original paper describes an older 80 percent training split with 10 percent each for validation and test; that holdout cannot certify the proposed checkpoint.

Original M3GNet and MACE-MP0 small source locations were identified, but no checkpoint-specific candidate exclusion crosswalk was recovered. Shared Materials Project ancestry alone is not an overlap count.
The pinned dataset README lists schema and split counts, without the required force conversion lineage or candidate-to-checkpoint split mapping. Model-side units do not complete that evidence.
limitations: No candidate outcomes decoded, panel selected, weights loaded or model predictions run. Source metadata is not measured checkpoint identity.
This bounded inspection is not an exhaustive search of all training archives. Neither independence nor a per-row contamination rate has been established.
The 800 reused archived cases remain exploratory. Historical A6 and failed/stopped model invocations retain their original states.
items.nextStep: Freeze a distinct archived-force analysis of shared, pairwise-aligned errors versus model disagreement on the original 800 cases. Use fixed residual identities and equal original group weights, independent arithmetic verification and no new predictions, ranking scores or generalization claim.

items.title: Offline guard binds cached force predictions to loaded model identity
items.summary: A tested prospective runner path now checks actual loaded state and inference settings before cache reuse or prediction, and preserves each cached prediction’s original producer. The first adapter is limited to CHGNet on CPU with legacy graph conversion. This is an offline workflow repair; no new model performance result was produced.
findings: All 133 focused offline runner, provenance and packaging checks passed using fake calculators and tiny fixtures. Independent adversarial review checked cache preservation and failure behavior.

Changed weights or effective settings, missing identity, incompatible caches and batch downgrades are rejected. Reused predictions retain their original producer; incomplete force outputs cannot be reported complete.
A distinct proposed study specifies 128 groups, one configuration per group, three model families, a fixed selection seed and fixed ranking decisions. It remains unstarted.
limitations: Real CHGNet runtime compatibility has not been accepted. The strict adapter covers package 0.4.2, CPU, baseline forces, legacy graph conversion and Distill off only; other model adapters remain unimplemented.
This repair does not identify historical weights, establish training independence or reference compatibility, prove cross-machine bitwise identity, or support concurrent checkpoint writers.
Candidate outcomes were not inspected, no panel was sampled, no real model loaded or predicted, and no runner image was deployed. Historical A6 remains INCONCLUSIVE.
items.nextStep: Prepare one checkpoint/provenance package per proposed model family plus one pinned reference/training-split packet. Produce a bounded readiness matrix, then either establish eligibility or stop this validation claim with the concrete incompatibility. All three adapters and real-runtime acceptance remain prerequisites.

items.title: Rank-only combination retains the average advantage over individual pairs
items.summary: Combining pair rankings without distance magnitudes beats every individual pair on both reused panels: +0.55 area percentage points on MatPES and +0.99 on OMat24 over the strongest pair. It does not consistently beat full disagreement.
findings: The fixed rank-fusion criterion passed on both panels. Original three-model force predictions and errors were unchanged.
Fusion minus full disagreement: -0.2629 area points on MatPES and +0.0367 on OMat24. No replacement score is selected.
Against the strongest pair, fusion improves 31/50 and 29/50 groups, and 137/400 and 184/400 configurations. Benefits are uneven.
Independent verification passed 106,518 numeric and 61,914 structural checks with no ranking, tie or sign-count discrepancies.
limitations: Historical, repeatedly inspected and correlated data; no independent holdout, calibrated alarm, novelty or generalization claim.
Fusion creates ties in 202/400 and 233/400 configurations. Magnitude removal also changes spacing and tie structure; no unique mechanism is isolated.
Ranking-area differences are not force-error reductions or cheaper inference. Exact training overlap and reference provenance remain incomplete.
Raw artifacts stay private; published hashes identify them without supplying public reproduction inputs. Historical A6 remains INCONCLUSIVE.
items.nextStep: Planned: audit a new validation panel for source identity, development-set disjointness, model checkpoints, reference settings and outcome-blind grouping. Freeze a separate test only if eligible; no further score variants on these 800 cases.

items.title: Full disagreement beats each pair on both archived panels
items.summary: With the original three-model prediction held fixed, full disagreement beats every pair in mean error-capture area. Its advantage over the strongest pair is 0.81 percentage points on MatPES and 0.95 on OMat24.
findings: The frozen all-pairs, both-panels criterion passed across 800 archived configurations and 100 recorded groups.
Against the strongest pair, full wins in 27 of 50 MatPES groups and 32 of 50 OMat groups; the mean gain is not uniform.
Independent verification passed 104,934 numeric and 47,521 structural checks, with no ranking or sign-count changes. Original predictions and errors were unchanged.
limitations: Historical correlated data; no independent holdout, calibration or generalization claim.
This changes error-ranking scores, not force accuracy or the cost of the three-model target prediction.
The full score is the sum of pair distances divided by nine. Pair rankings and magnitudes may both contribute.
Raw artifacts remain private; hashes provide traceability, not public reproduction inputs. Historical A6 remains INCONCLUSIVE.
items.nextStep: Planned: combine within-configuration pair midranks with equal weights, preserving exact ties, and test whether a positive mean advantage over every pair survives without raw score magnitudes.

items.summary: Disagreement improves equal-group mean error-capture area over the force-magnitude control on both panels: +2.04 percentage points on MatPES and +1.34 on OMat24. About half of individual configurations improve.
findings: The fixed positive-mean criterion passed on both panels. Positive groups: 37 of 50 and 29 of 50.
Positive configurations: 208 of 400 and 207 of 400. These are ranking gains, not reductions in force error.
Six archived files matched recorded hashes. Independent verification passed 42,954 numeric and 8,962 structural checks.
limitations: Historical correlated archive data; not a new sealed held-out benchmark.
CHGNet, M3GNet and MACE-MP-small differ from the pilot roster. Reference settings and training overlap remain incomplete.
No novelty, calibration, deployment-alarm or generalization claim. Historical A6 remains INCONCLUSIVE.

items.summary: Disagreement ranked error above the uniform-subset baseline on four of five configurations but beat the force-magnitude control on only three. The strict all-five criterion failed.
findings: Independent arithmetic verification passed 586 checks.
One configuration was nearly uninformative; it does not establish a significant failure mode.
limitations: Tiny previously inspected sample; no novelty, calibration or generalization claim.
